title: docs(guide): point ci-cd-pipeline.md's populations at what derives them, instead of counting them
body:
Fixes #8629 (objectui#8629).

## What was wrong

Three sentences on `content/docs/guide/ci-cd-pipeline.md` stated a live population as a literal with nothing deriving it:

| where | what it stated | what derives it |
|:--|:--|:--|
| the eager-closure section, on the `/docs/[[...slug]]` route | a docs-page population, `all 181 docs pages` | the docs collection directory `apps/site/source.config.ts` declares |
| the shell-escape section, on the `skills` scan root | a file population, `16 files stayed behind` | `SCAN_ROOTS`, re-read by the gate on every run |
| the half-state patrol section | the sweeper's page window, `4 pages` | `CLOSED_ISSUE_WINDOW_PAGES`, exported by the sweeper |

The first was **measurably false**: re-measured on this branch, that corpus is **184** git-tracked `.md`/`.mdx` files against **181** claimed. The second and third were true when the card was filed and are true today — and that is the point, since nothing in CI could go red over any of the three.

## What changed

⛔ **The numbers are not corrected.** A corrected count with nothing checking it is the same card a month later, which is the ruling objectui#7448, objectui#7825 and objectui#7965 each recorded after doing exactly that. Each sentence now names the tree its population comes from and the run that prints the live reading — the eager-closure gate's `gauge:` line, the residue gate's per-root `N file(s), N fence(s)` line, and the sweeper's exported constant by name. `ci-cd-pipeline-doc.test.ts` gains one pin per section that refuses a count written back, each with positive controls so a moved or emptied section fails loudly instead of passing vacuously, plus parity assertions that the readings the page now points at actually exist.

### Departure from objectui#8606's shape, stated because the dispatch asked for it

objectui#8606 landed the same decision on a workflow header hours earlier: delete the count, say in the header why none is stated, point at the directory the population is derived from. This follows it on all three counts. Two deliberate differences, both because a published guide is not a comment block:

- **The prose keeps its argument.** The eager-closure sentence exists to say the route is shared, not to report a size, so it now says `every docs page shares` and moves the population question to the derivation. A guide sentence that reads as a gate's disclaimer would be worse prose than the one it replaced.
- **The third member is pointed at, not deleted.** Its value is a copied constant that is currently *true*, so there is nothing stale to delete; naming the export removes the copy while leaving the value where its argument lives.

### ⛔ What was deliberately not touched

- **The four correct neighbours.** Sentences that state the commit or window they were measured on — the skills-paths guide-file measurement, the test-file/test-count cell (itself an earlier card's remedy, already survived one drift), the first-parent-commit window on changeset overwrites, and the fields-page figure. Rewriting any of them into a live figure would *create* this defect. That is why the new pins are section-scoped: a page-wide ban on `N files` would flag exactly those.
- **objectui#8606's workflow header** — landed, and a different file surface.
- **The doc-parity test's inventory and command-parity assertions** — objectui#8726's and objectui#8420's surfaces, both queued behind this card on the same page.
- **objectui#7966's open noun-set question.** Whether a `pages?` noun that means *paginated API result pages* belongs to the family at all is that card's ruling, not this one's. The third member is handled in a way that survives either answer: the pin holds only the local fact that a constant copied into prose rots when the export moves, and its comment says so.

## ⭐ The unit, which is the transferable half

Both defective sentences **wrap** — the numeral ends one line and its noun begins the next — so a per-line reader returns **zero** for sentences that are plainly present on the page. That was measured twice before this branch existed (by the seat verifying the card, and by objectui#8606 from the workflow side), and it is why two of the three were invisible to the census that went looking for them.

Every assertion here therefore judges **joined** text, and the pin proves its own unit rather than asserting it: it searches the page for three consecutive words that straddle a line break, then asserts both halves — the phrase **is** in the joined text and is in **no** single line. If the page ever stops wrapping, that control goes undefined and says so, instead of quietly degrading to a per-line-equivalent reader.

## Verification

Run on the merged tree; the numbers below are from the final commit, `2357815b7`.

- `vitest run --project unit scripts/__tests__/ci-cd-pipeline-doc.test.ts` — **73 passed** (70 pre-existing + 3 new pins + the unit control, in one new block).
- `pnpm type-check:scripts` — exit 0. `check-doc-links`, `check-control-bytes`, `check-new-line-citations`, `check-doc-fences`, `check-changeset-presence`, `check-shell-escape-residue`, `check-docs-route-closure`, `check-skills-paths` — all exit 0.
- `eslint` on the changed test file: 1 file, 0 errors, 0 warnings. The repo-wide flat invocation (`eslint . --no-inline-config`, 4743 files) reports 95 errors across 79 files, none of them touched here and none under `scripts/`; that flat form is not this repo's lint entry point (`turbo run lint` is).

### Ablation — each new pin proven able to fail

Each mutation was committed-state-relative: written to disk, the write proven by a fixed-string grep and by the file's blob hash diverging from its `HEAD` blob, then restored with `git checkout HEAD --` and the restore proven by an empty `git diff HEAD` and the blob hash returning to `8bb95acdb`.

| mutation | result |
|:--|:--|
| a docs-page count written back into the eager-closure section the "states no docs-page population" pin fails; 72 pass |
| a `skills` file count written back into the shell-escape section the "states no skills file population" pin fails; 72 pass |
| the page window copied back into the half-state section the "copies no page window out of the sweeper" pin fails; 72 pass |

⭐ A fourth ablation demonstrates the trap directly: the same count injected so that it **wraps** (`all 184` ending one line, `docs pages share` opening the next). `grep -cF '184 docs pages'` returns **0** — a per-line reader calls that page clean — while the pin reddens with `found "184 docs pages"`.

## Out of scope, filed

objectui#9004 — a fourth stated docs-page population on this page (`556-page docs build`), hyphenated and singular, so objectui#7448's noun pattern does not match it; the same figure is mirrored in the gate's own header, outside `content/docs/**`. Widening that pattern touches every carrier of the family, so this branch records the gap in the pin's comment rather than widening it unilaterally.

Also observed, not filed: the same section family carries a closed-card figure whose noun (`cards`) is outside the family's noun set entirely — reported to the dispatching seat rather than filed, because its class membership depends on objectui#7966's open ruling.

## Changeset

Empty frontmatter, declared explicitly: no package `src/` is touched, so this publishes nothing.

⛔ Draft on purpose — not flipped ready, not enqueued, no auto-merge.
